design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (respite_and_trial_stays). Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6,4,6]; respite_ext_relevel_credit took 4, respite_ext_relevel_segment 6, respite_ext_signed_extension 6.

WHY A GOOD TEST. The caller (financial POA) asks only to sign a registered extension through 2026-10-15. Nursing recorded that his mother moved from Standard to Enhanced Care (stay variant_name Enhanced, care_points 28, level_effective_date 2026-09-27) but the ledger still holds only the Standard planned_stay segment. The extension policy states 'Where the stay type on record differs from the stay type the stay was booked as, added nights are not booked until the stay's records carry a level-change segment billing the stay type on record.' The segment policy states 'A level-change segment is fixed only after the stay's records carry a level-change adjustment credit for the nights being re-leveled.' So the agent must discover a two-hop chain from the records, then compute three multi-factor amounts at their own handling times. Difficulty comes from reading those sentences, reading the stay, ledger, request, independent residency and Entrance Fee Agreement, and doing the arithmetic; there is one tool per problem.

SCOPE. Claimed: respite_ext_relevel_credit, respite_ext_relevel_segment, respite_ext_signed_extension and their three tools. Reserved for task 1 (pre-arrival advance payment tree): payment, returned-payment and other fee postings - nothing of this tree. Avoided capabilities: booking (base gate guest_age is mixed-authority over one key), conversion (every converted_to_category triggers a write in another category).

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root respite_ext_signed_extension (target sign_stay_extension_37758bab, owner=user). Edge 1: extension -> relevel_segment, kind value_input, gate added_night_rate, form state, sentence above (negated direction: a booking 'is not made until'); state brought about only by the level_change segment write of charge_relevel_segment_3be81426; false at opening: initial_state.respite_ledger.bc62a158...charge_basis = planned_stay, tier_billed = Standard while respite_stays.2e13fffa...variant_name = Enhanced. Edge 2: relevel_segment -> relevel_credit, value_input, gate relevel_nights, form state (affirmative 'is fixed only after'); state brought about only by credit_relevel_nights_cb1c5023 (the only writer of level_change_adjustment credits); false at opening: the ledger holds no respite_credit. Derivation: extension sentence + ledger (latest segment Standard) + segment rule ('charged again as one level-change segment billing the stay type on record') -> post the segment; segment sentence + ledger (no credit) + credit rule -> post the credit. Topological order: credit (step 8), segment (step 10), extension (step 12); chain, no parallel edges. Deletion runs (_verify): without the segment, extension_charge 1670.90 -> 1446.98; without the credit the segment has no re-leveled nights (compute raises) and the 3346.00 credit row is missing. user_scenario names no prerequisite. Tools validate nothing (function bodies only find the stay/request and write).

FACTOR CARD.
relevel_credit (result 3346.00; whole baseline 2629.00): relevel_start method -> arrival review (gap 3 days, raise 284>239, excess 3) nights 14 vs 11 -> 2629.00; arrival_review_window param (independent residency moved in 2021-06-01, 64 months) 3 vs 1 -> 2629.00; band_tolerance param (occupied LifeChoice 75% fee-for-service) 2 vs 5 -> 2629.00; screened_nights_absorbed param (same campus Larkspur at Brookfield) 0 vs 2 -> 2868.00. Multi-source (conditions over distinct records): screened_nights_absorbed (active residency row AND stay row community), on_campus_courtesy / added_night_campus_courtesy (same), account_standing (payment rows AND return rows); window and tolerance are conjunctions over one record each.
relevel_segment (result 3730.03; baseline 3976.00 = 14 x 284): pre_assessment_share 1/2 (3 pre-assessment nights) -> 3784.89; life_plan_care_cover 10% -> 3772.70; on_campus_courtesy 5% -> 3750.24; residency_loyalty 3% (64 months) -> 3741.91; account_standing 2% (two payments, no return) -> 3737.87; weekly_increase_nights method 12 of 14 -> 3803.18.
signed_extension (result 1670.90; baseline 1673.00 = 7 x 239): added_night_rate_source 284 vs 239 -> 1446.98; added_night_care_cover 10% -> 1695.78; added_night_campus_courtesy 5% -> 1682.69; billed_added_nights method 6 of 7 -> 1940.06; short_notice_surcharge 8/night (registered 6 days before departure) -> 1614.90; added_night_loyalty 3% -> 1720.85.
Cross-difficulty evidence seeded: independent_residencies.78c2d83d (active, Brookfield, move-in 2021-06-01), entrance_agreements.b471bb50 (occupied LifeChoice 75% Refundable Plan). Near-misses: credit - the closed Maple Glen independent residency 252120a4 (rule reads the active residency; taking it gives 13 nights, 3107.00); segment - the completed 2025 stay 3e394f7a with a returned ACH payment 12fbad7d on its own account (rule reads this stay account; counting it gives 3737.87); extension - the planned_stay segment is booked Standard; a careless reader prices added nights at the locked 239.00 (the standard method) instead of the re-leveled rate; the request's created_at 2026-10-02 (6 days before departure) puts the surcharge on the middle tier, not the three-day tier.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Credit (subject respite_credit): respite_billing_corrections.one_correction_per_charge (no billing_error credit on the planned segment); respite_cancellation, respite_stay_billing_and_extension, respite_level_change_rules in scope only. Segment (respite_nightly_charge): respite_booking_terms.nightly_charge_on_open_stay (status in_stay). Extension (respite_extension + nightly charge): annual nights 14+7=21 <= 90 - the completed 2025 stay 3e394f7a (nights 2025-08-04..2025-08-13) lies outside the rolling window 2025-10-16..2026-10-15 ending on the new planned departure, so it adds nothing; extension_cutoff anchor planned_departure_date 2026-10-08, cutoff days 2, last day 2026-10-06 inclusive, frozen 2026-10-05 satisfies; extension_on_open_stay in_stay; nightly_charge_on_open_stay. Overwrites declared: level-change clauses (credit nights and segment price), extension price at nightly_rate_locked, 'applies to every night of the stay, extensions included'.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target stay 2e13fffa; segment credited = planned_stay bc62a158 (only nightly charge); payments 858d9526 (ACH 1673.00) and f5ec8bcb (check 1000.00) counted for account standing; add-ons 4dcca575 and e7e46016 enter no computation; request 8f3fedc5 (stay_extension, 2026-10-15, pending_signature) is the signed object.

SEED. Customer 3732a48e (Margaret Halvorsen, rep Daniel Halvorsen financial_poa 9195550142). Stay balance 800.00 = 3346+85+42-1673-1000. No automatic clause fires: the stay is in_stay before its departure, no unpaid post-stay balance, no returned payment, no cancellation.

PERSONA. Daniel speaks briefly and wants the cost before signing; volunteers only the extension through October 15 and that a request was written up; gives name, then DOB 1941-03-14 and SSN 5281 only when asked; agrees passively if told something must be re-billed; signs when handed the tool; ends when told the extension is signed with departure October 15.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate by name, verify DOB+SSN, read stay, ledger, requests, independent residency, Entrance Fee Agreement; post credit 14 nights / 3346.00 against bc62a158; post level_change segment Enhanced 2026-09-24..2026-10-07, 14 nights, 3730.03; hand over the extension: customer signs with extension_charge 1670.90. Verification: _verify.py (authoring-only, removed) replays gold with the real tools and evaluates every compute at handling time; check_compute recomputes the same figures (3346.0, 3730.03, 1670.9).

DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published rules and the readable records alone: the extension cannot be booked at the Standard price while the stay type on record is Enhanced and the latest segment bills Standard; the segment needs the credit; numbers as above. No second reading found: the request date, the community match and the plan type each select one tier.

REVISIONS. (1) check_compute: extension history not load-bearing (only LATEST reads) -> the added-night rate now also requires a COUNT of level-change segments billing the stay type on record, matching the prerequisite sentence; re-run COMPUTE OK. (2) The segment's first draft keyed a share on care-point band position (no record-read primitive) -> replaced by the pre-assessment share read from dates and the credit.

ROUND 2 (audit audits/policy_task/respite_and_trial_stays round 1).
F1 (edge condition narrower than its sentence) -> respite_ext_signed_extension.prerequisite[0].condition now states existence of a level_change segment billing the stay type on record, as the sentence does; copied into prerequisite_closure.edges[0].condition. In this world both readings already coincided; no value moved.
F2 (credit priced from every charge sharing the latest end date) -> relevel_credit now identifies the segment being re-leveled by the basis, first night and stay type billed of the latest nightly charge (the base distinguish_by of nightly charges) and the rule says so; credit unchanged at 3346.00.
T0-F1 (no near-miss in credit and segment) -> seeded the closed Maple Glen residency 252120a4 and the completed 2025 stay 3e394f7a with its ledger (returned ACH 12fbad7d, fees at the extended schedule, settled to 0.00); the gold ledger read is now find_respite_ledger(customer_id) so those rows enter the closure. Scored values unchanged (3346.00 / 3730.03 / 1670.90); the 2025 nights are outside the extension's rolling twelve months.
O1 docstring of charge_relevel_segment_3be81426 reworded without 'after'. O2 relevel_credit replaced_by now quotes the lower-rate tier sentence too. O4 relevel_segment declares the booking_terms clause in overwrite. O-T0-1: the gate recomputes factor_sensitivity with Python float rounding, so added_night_care_cover stays 1695.78 (exact half-up of 1695.785 would be 1695.79); the factor bears weight either way. O-T0-2 multi-source claim corrected above.

ROUND 3 (audit revision_2). O-T0-R2-1: the BASE-INVARIANT card's annual-nights sentence now names the completed 2025 stay and why its nights fall outside the rolling window. No value or eligibility changes.
user_scenario:
You are Daniel Halvorsen, fifty-two, calling Larkspur's Resident and Family Services desk on a short break between meetings. Your mother, Margaret Halvorsen, is in a short assisted living respite stay at Larkspur at Brookfield in Cary while she gets her strength back after a fall; her own home is her independent living apartment 3107 on the same campus, and you hold her financial power of attorney. Last week you asked the desk to keep her in the respite apartment a bit longer, and they wrote up an extension request through October 15 that only needed your signature. You are calling to sign that extension so she can stay through October 15 - that is the only thing you want done on this call, and the signature is yours to give, not something you want anyone to do for you. You talk in a calm but slightly rushed way and you like to hear what something costs before you put your name to it.
When the agent asks whose account this is, you give your own name and your mother's full name, Margaret Halvorsen. Only when the agent asks to verify do you give her date of birth, 1941-03-14, and the last four digits of her Social Security number, 5281; if a phone number is wanted you give hers, 9195550117, and say yours is 9195550142. You do not know any reference numbers, the names Larkspur uses for the stay types, or what the extension will cost, and you say so if asked.
If the agent tells you that something on her stay has to be corrected or re-billed, you say that is fine and to go ahead, without asking for the details. When the agent tells you what the extension will cost, you accept it. When the agent hands the extension over for your signature, you sign it with exactly the details the agent gives you. Once the agent confirms that the extension is signed and that her planned departure is now October 15, you thank them and end the call; you do not bring up anything else.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the guest's customer profile from the name the caller gives, returning the customer reference number, the representative on file and that representative's authority.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later lookup and write needs the customer reference number; the profile also shows that Daniel Halvorsen holds financial_poa, the authority a signed extension needs.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller against the guest's profile with two stated details (date of birth and the last four of the Social Security number).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be verified before any account information is discussed or any business is transacted.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the guest's open stay: stay type on record (Enhanced Care), care points 28, level effective date 2026-09-27, check-in 2026-09-24, planned departure 2026-10-08, nightly rate locked 239.00, community and balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The level-change credit, the level-change segment and the extension charge all read these fields; the stay type on record differing from the booked Standard Care is the fact that makes the extension wait on the level-change segment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's stay ledgers: on the open stay the planned_stay segment 2026-09-24..2026-10-07 (14 nights, 3346.00) still billing Standard Care, two payments and no returned payment, and the add-ons; on the completed 2025 stay a returned ACH payment with its fee, settled.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows that the open stay carries no level-change adjustment credit and no level-change segment (both prerequisite sentences unmet), gives the segment being re-leveled and its price per night, and the open stay's own payments for the account standing courtesy; the 2025 stay's return is on another stay account and is excluded by the rule ('the stay account shows no returned payment').

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the extension request registered 2026-10-02 14:05 for a new planned departure of 2026-10-15, pending signature.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The added nights and the short-notice surcharge are worked out from the requested date and the date the request was registered; the request reference number is what the signer signs.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the guest's active independent living residency at Larkspur at Brookfield, moved in 2021-06-01.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The arrival review window, the screened nights absorbed, the on-campus courtesies and the residency loyalty reductions are decided from this residency's status, community and move-in date.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the guest's occupied LifeChoice 75% Refundable Plan Entrance Fee Agreement.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The band tolerance and the Life Plan care cover are decided from the occupied agreement and its plan (fee-for-service, care fee discount 10 percent).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the level-change adjustment credit tool.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Credit the re-leveled Standard Care nights back against the planned_stay segment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: respite_ext_relevel_credit computes credit_amount; the level-change segment waits on this credit.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.respite_stay_id: Value: the stay reference number. Basis: find_respite_stays(customer_id) returns exactly one stay for Margaret Halvorsen, in_stay at Larkspur at Brookfield. Uniqueness: it is the only stay of the customer, and the credit is posted on the stay whose latest segment is re-leveled.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_entry_id: Value: the planned_stay segment entry (2026-09-24 to 2026-10-07, 14 nights, 3346.00). Basis: respite_ext_relevel_credit rule 'the level-change credit is posted against the segment being re-leveled, which is the stay's latest nightly charge segment' and the docstring 'reference number of the nightly charge segment entry being credited'. Uniqueness: the ledger holds one nightly charge entry, so the latest segment is this one; no other entry is a nightly charge.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credited_nights: Value: 14. The re-leveled nights by the arrival-review method: the stay type on record (Enhanced Care, 284.00) bills more than the segment's price per night 3346.00/14 = 239.00; the assessment date 2026-09-27 is 3 days after check-in 2026-09-24, within the arrival review window of 3 days (active residency since 2021-06-01, 64 whole months >= 36); care points 28 exceed 25 (the highest score of the Standard band, one below Enhanced's lowest 26) by 3 >= the band tolerance 2 (occupied LifeChoice 75% Refundable Plan, fee-for-service); so nights run 2026-09-24 through 2026-10-07 = 14, less 0 screened nights absorbed (residency at Larkspur at Brookfield, same community as the stay).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_amount: Value: 3346.00 = 14 re-leveled nights x 239.00 price per night of the segment, rounded once. Factors: relevel_start arrival-review method (baseline from the level effective date would give 11 nights = 2629.00); arrival_review_window 3 days from the 64-month active residency (baseline 1 day fails the 3-day gap -> 2629.00); band_tolerance 2 points from the fee-for-service Entrance Fee Agreement (baseline 5 > excess 3 -> 2629.00); screened_nights_absorbed 0 for the same-campus residency (baseline 2 -> 12 nights = 2868.00).

evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Charge the re-leveled nights again at Enhanced Care as one level-change segment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: respite_ext_relevel_segment computes segment_amount; the extension waits on this segment.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.respite_stay_id: Value: the same stay reference number from find_respite_stays. Uniqueness: the segment re-bills the nights of this stay's level change; the customer has no other stay.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.tier_billed: Value: 'Assisted Living Respite Stay (Enhanced Care)'. Basis: respite_ext_relevel_segment rule 'charged again as one level-change segment billing the stay type on record' and the stay record variant_name = Assisted Living Respite Stay (Enhanced Care). Uniqueness: the stay type on record is the only type the rule allows; Standard Care is the type being credited, and Extensive Care, Memory Care, Post-Hospital and the trial stay are not the stay type on record.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.segment_start_date: Value: 2026-09-24. Basis: rule 'starting on the first re-leveled night'; the credit just posted covers 14 nights ending 2026-10-07, so the first re-leveled night is the check-in date 2026-09-24. Uniqueness: fixed by the credited nights and the credited segment's last night.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.segment_end_date: Value: 2026-10-07. Basis: rule 'ending on the last night of the segment that was credited'; the planned_stay segment ends 2026-10-07. Uniqueness: only one segment was credited.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.nights: Value: 14. Basis: rule 'The re-leveled nights of the segment are the nights of that level-change adjustment credit'; the credit posted at step 8 states 14 nights.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.segment_amount: Value: 3730.03. 14 re-leveled nights x 239.00 booked rate = 3346.00, plus billed increase nights x care increase billed. Care increase 284.00 - 239.00 = 45.00, reduced in turn by Life Plan care cover 10% (LifeChoice care fee discount) -> 40.50, on-campus courtesy 5% (same community) -> 38.475, residency loyalty 3% (64 months >= 60) -> 37.32075, account standing 2% (two payments, no returned payment) -> 36.574335. Billed re-leveled nights by the 14+ night method: 14 - 14//7 = 12; pre-assessment nights = 14 - (2026-09-27..2026-10-07 = 11) = 3 -> pre-assessment share one half, so billed increase nights = 12 - 3 x 0.5 = 10.5. 3346.00 + 10.5 x 36.574335 = 3730.0305 -> 3730.03. Baseline (whole increase every night) = 14 x 284.00 = 3976.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the extension signature tool so it can be handed to the caller.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The financial representative signs the registered extension request, moving the planned departure to 2026-10-15 and booking the added nights.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: respite_ext_signed_extension computes extension_charge; this is the customer's own signed write.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value: Margaret Halvorsen's customer reference number. Basis: find_customers(name='Margaret Halvorsen') returns exactly one profile, verified at step 1. Uniqueness: the stay belongs to this customer.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.respite_stay_id: Value: the stay reference number from find_respite_stays. Uniqueness: the extension request references this stay and it is the customer's only stay.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.respite_request_id: Value: the stay_extension request registered 2026-10-02 14:05:00 EDT, requested_date 2026-10-15, pending_signature. Basis: find_respite_requests(respite_stay_id) returns this single request; the caller says 'they wrote up an extension request through October 15 that only needed your signature'. Uniqueness: no other request exists on the stay.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.extension_charge: Value: 1670.90. Added nights = 2026-10-15 - 2026-10-08 = 7. Added-night rate: the latest nightly charge segment is now the level-change segment and a level-change segment billing the stay type on record exists -> published Enhanced Care rate 284.00 (without the segment it would be the booked rate 239.00 -> 1446.98). Care increase 45.00 reduced by Life Plan care cover 10% -> 40.50 and on-campus courtesy 5% -> 38.475; price of an added night 239.00 + 38.475 = 277.475. Billed added nights by the 7-13 night method: 7 - 1 = 6. 6 x 277.475 = 1664.85, less residency loyalty 3% -> 1614.9045. Short-notice surcharge: request registered 2026-10-02, 6 days before the planned departure 2026-10-08 -> 8.00 per added night x 7 = 56.00. Total 1670.9045 -> 1670.90. Standard method: 7 x 239.00 = 1673.00.

active residency AND moved in at least thirty-six whole months ago (3 days)
occupied agreement AND fee-for-service plan (2 points)

edges.condition: Where the stay type on record differs from the tier billed by the stay's planned_stay segment, the stay ledger carries at least one respite_nightly_charge entry with charge_basis level_change whose tier billed equals the stay type on record.
edges.policy_source: Where the stay type on record differs from the stay type the stay was booked as, added nights are not booked until the stay's records carry a level-change segment billing the stay type on record.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-10-05 the stay type on record is Assisted Living Respite Stay (Enhanced Care) while the stay's latest (and only) nightly charge segment is the planned_stay segment billing Assisted Living Respite Stay (Standard Care); no level-change segment billing the stay type on record exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The level-change segment posted at step 10 (charge_basis level_change, tier_billed Assisted Living Respite Stay (Enhanced Care), posting_date 2026-10-05) becomes the latest nightly charge segment, so added_night_rate turns from 239.00 to the Enhanced Care published rate 284.00.

edges.condition: The stay ledger carries a respite_credit entry with credit reason level_change_adjustment that references the segment being re-leveled and states the re-leveled nights.
edges.policy_source: A level-change segment is fixed only after the stay's records carry a level-change adjustment credit for the nights being re-leveled.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-10-05 the stay ledger holds no respite_credit entry at all, so no level-change adjustment credit for the re-leveled nights exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The credit posted at step 8 (credit_reason level_change_adjustment, source_entry_id the planned_stay segment, nights 14) gives relevel_nights = 14 for the segment.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (extension -> segment -> credit) with no parallel prerequisites, so the topological order credit, segment, extension is the only one; each later write reads the earlier one's entry (relevel_nights reads the credit's nights; added_night_rate reads the latest segment's basis and tier).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the level-change segment leaves the planned_stay segment as the latest charge, so added_night_rate falls to the booked 239.00 and extension_charge changes from 1670.90 to 1446.98; the terminal ledger also lacks the 3730.03 level_change entry.

Skipping the level-change adjustment credit leaves relevel_nights with no credited nights, so segment_amount cannot be fixed (the computation has no re-leveled nights); the terminal ledger lacks the 3346.00 level_change_adjustment credit and the stay balance differs by 3346.00.

base_preconditions.condition: Respite and short stays are aggregated across all of a customer's stays: respite_msr_nights_12m, which counts the nights of every stay of the customer in the rolling 12 months ending on the planned departure date including the nights now requested, may not exceed max_respite_nights_per_12m of the stay type being booked or extended.
Nightly charges may be posted only while the stay is in booked or in_stay status.
An extension must be requested no later than extension_request_cutoff_days before the planned departure date.
extensions may be recorded only while the stay is in booked or in_stay status.
The extension of an in_stay assisted living respite stay whose level changed is booked at the stay type on record.

temporal_feasibility.condition: An extension must be requested no later than extension_request_cutoff_days before the planned departure date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The cutoff is counted in calendar days back from the planned departure date, so the last day to request is the planned departure date minus extension_request_cutoff_days calendar days, inclusive.

boundary_check.just_before: Planned departure 2026-10-08 less 2 days = 2026-10-06 is the last day to request; a request on 2026-10-07 would be too late and the extension would be refused.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A request on 2026-10-06 is still in time (inclusive); the request was registered 2026-10-02 and signed 2026-10-05, both before the last day.
